summary: In a 3+-class differing-type chain (e.g. C(v: str) extends B(v: str) extends A(v: int)), the first-seen-vs-current comparison reports the outermost conflicting pair (C vs A) and never names the intermediate class B, even though B shares C's own type and sits between the two named classes in the MRO.
note: Confirmed by re-reading check_incompatible_attribute_redeclarations's comparison loop: correctness is unaffected (a genuine conflict is always caught and rejected with T0052; no differing-type redeclaration can pass silently), and the gap is limited to which class names appear in the diagnostic message for a 3+-class chain. Tracking per-attribute provenance through arbitrary-length chains to name every intermediate class would add real bookkeeping complexity for a rare, message-quality-only benefit. Recorded as reviewed with no fix.
